title: A reported airspace violation can move from national interception to alliance posture without proving deterrence
source_unit: Official NATO and Polish government accounts of the September 2025 Polish airspace incident and Eastern Sentry response
geography: Poland and NATO eastern flank; September 2025 airspace incident

observations.period: September 9-10, 2025; reported Russian-drone airspace violation and immediate response

denominator.unit: official incident-and-response account involving multiple reported drones

incident.value: Polish and NATO records report repeated violations of Polish airspace by Russian drones during the night of September 9-10, creating territorial, civilian, infrastructure, and aviation-safety risk

national_response.value: Polish defensive procedures were activated and threatening drones were intercepted; Poland requested Article 4 consultations

independent_effect.unit: missing independent attribution, complete object-level count, damage, civilian exposure, interception cost, readiness burden, and deterrence outcome

observations.method: Structured extraction from official NATO and Polish government statements; the record separates reported operational action from independent incident verification and later effects.
observations.uncertainty: Official statements do not provide an independent attribution audit, complete damage or object-level denominator, civilian-risk estimate, interception cost, or counterfactual for what would have occurred without the response.
observations.subgroup: Polish territory, NATO eastern-flank defense institutions, affected civil-aviation and civilian systems, and the foreign actor identified in official accounts; no individual civilian sample is supplied.
observations.counterinterpretation: A successful interception and Article 4 request can show that response procedures functioned without proving the origin, intent, civilian protection, or strategic consequence of the incident.

observations.period: September 12, 2025 and after; Eastern Sentry, allied support, diplomacy, and information-resilience response

alliance_response.value: NATO announced Eastern Sentry and additional eastern-flank support after the incident; Poland pursued diplomatic protest and public-information responses

institutional_sequence.value: The episode advanced from tactical interception to Article 4 consultation, allied solidarity, strengthened posture, diplomatic action, and information-resilience messaging

durable_effect.unit: missing deployment duration, equipment and troop counts, local burden, public approval, budget change, later foreign-actor behavior, and civilian-security outcome

mechanism.value: A security incident can become a multi-domain governance episode in which operational defense, alliance legitimacy, diplomacy, and information control move on different clocks; announced posture is not the same as deterrence or durable public consent

observations.method: Structured extraction from official NATO and Polish government response statements; announced actions are retained as reported institutional stages rather than treated as measured effects.
observations.uncertainty: The public response record does not establish actual deployment duration, readiness, fiscal or local burden, audience belief, later Russian behavior, or whether the posture changed the probability of another incursion.
observations.subgroup: NATO member governments, Polish public institutions, eastern-flank defense structures, host communities, and audiences of official information; no linked public-opinion or cost denominator is reported.
observations.counterinterpretation: An announced reinforcement can be procedural reassurance or political signaling without proving increased readiness, deterrence, civilian security, or durable alliance legitimacy.

boundary: This record establishes a reported Poland/NATO incident-to-response sequence from airspace violation through interception, Article 4 consultation, Eastern Sentry, diplomacy, and information-resilience action. It does not establish independent attribution, deterrence, actual deployment effect, public legitimacy, civilian security, or later foreign-actor behavior.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The hash covers the compact project event ledger derived from the official NATO and Polish source accounts; classified operational files, civilian incident records, and independent damage or attribution datasets are not retained.
